targets.approach: From the small dirt pull-in beside the road, just before it runs under the face, walk north to a low ridge that rises west toward the bluff. Keep going to a very large black oak, then contour left through the woods around to the base of the wall. The old trail from the days of route development has grown over, so expect to find the way by eye. Antithesis begins under a slender, left-rising roof; Innervisions and Right-A-This begin next to it.
targets.name: Antithesis

targets.name: Your Secret's Safe with Me

targets.approach: Park near the Hungover Wall on Keller Peak Road and walk uphill, cross the road, and head south at an open area. Descend through a seasonal stream bed and climb the steep hillside on the far side until the formation comes into view, then continue uphill and round its right side to avoid heavy brush. Beef Kabob is a thin crack at the right edge of the west face, right of a prominent roof.
targets.name: Beef Kabob

targets.approach: Park near the Hungover Wall on Keller Peak Road and walk uphill, cross the road, and head south at an open area. Fish Sticks is a hand-sized crack on the sunny south face.
targets.name: Fish Sticks

targets.approach: Park near the Hungover Wall on Keller Peak Road and walk uphill, cross the road, and head south at an open area. Descend through a seasonal stream bed and climb the steep hillside on the far side until the formation comes into view, then continue uphill and round its right side to avoid heavy brush. P.B.O. Crack is the prominent offwidth near the left end of the west face.
targets.name: P.B.O. Crack

targets.approach: From a campsite at Peeler Lake, walk up a grassy drainage to the east and the wall appears on the left. Ledges form the lower half of the wall and can be scrambled to the halfway ledge where the main-section routes begin. Bold Deceiver climbs the two striking cracks in the orange face at the right-hand end of the main wall.
targets.descent_text: Belay on gear at the top, then walk left to the main ledge and follow the walk-off. Walk off down the gully between the two subsections of the wall.
targets.name: Bold Deceiver

targets.approach: From a campsite at Peeler Lake, walk up a grassy drainage to the east and the wall appears on the left. Ledges form the lower half of the wall and can be scrambled to the halfway ledge where the main-section routes begin. Money Don't Grow on Trees climbs the big corner that faces right at the extreme right end of the wall, entered by an easy scramble or chimney from the left.
targets.descent_text: Belay on gear above the corner and walk off to the left.
targets.name: Money Don't Grow on Trees

targets.approach: From a campsite at Peeler Lake, walk up a grassy drainage to the east and the wall appears on the left. Ledges form the lower half of the wall and can be scrambled to the halfway ledge where the main-section routes begin. No Bed of Roses is the hand crack next to Rosie, Sweet Rosie on its left; it runs into a patch of dark rock a short way up.
targets.descent_text: Walk off down the gully between the two subsections of the wall.
targets.name: No Bed of Roses

targets.approach: From a campsite at Peeler Lake, walk up a grassy drainage to the east and the wall appears on the left. Ledges form the lower half of the wall and can be scrambled to the halfway ledge where the main-section routes begin. Rosie, Sweet Rosie is the first route in the wall's right-hand section, immediately beyond the descent gully, and begins up a big flake facing left.
targets.descent_text: Belay on gear on the large ledge at the top and walk off to the left.
targets.name: Rosie, Sweet Rosie

targets.approach: From a campsite at Peeler Lake, walk up a grassy drainage to the east and the wall appears on the left. Ledges form the lower half of the wall and can be scrambled to the halfway ledge where the main-section routes begin. Stand and Deceiver begins up Stand and Deliver and finishes on Bold Deceiver, so it uses the center of the right side and then moves right to the upper crack.
targets.descent_text: Walk off down the gully between the two subsections of the wall.
targets.name: Stand and Deceiver

targets.approach: Drive to the top of Pine Creek where the pack station is, and start up the Pine Creek Pass trail. Pipe Wall sits beside the trail and is the first of the Brownstone walls you meet. Starting from the big slab at the foot of the wall, scramble up and to the right, past a corner facing right, to the foot of the next corner; the route is the thin crack in the left side of that corner's left wall.
targets.name: Somebody Stop Me

targets.approach: From the southern parking lot at the Holcomb Valley Pinnacles, walk east from the fence line to a south-facing formation with a single bolt in the middle of its face. New Pygmy goes up the layered plates at the formation's left end and finishes on a slab.
targets.name: New Pygmy

targets.approach: From the southern parking lot at the Holcomb Valley Pinnacles, walk east from the fence line to a south-facing formation with a single bolt in the middle of its face. Watusi Rodeo follows the seam that angles up and left on the right side of the formation.
targets.name: Watusi Rodeo

targets.approach: There are two ways in. The direct one follows the approach used for the Mean Streak wall, then cuts left up to the base of the buttress. The longer, gentler one climbs the Pine Creek Pass trail to the Brownstone buttress, leaves the trail slightly downhill at the end of the long switchback below it, crosses Pine Creek below the waterfall, and heads up the open shelf that cuts up right toward the buttress, following occasional cairns across open ground. The route is the obvious lightning-bolt dihedral in the middle of the white quartz-streaked buttress.
targets.descent_text: Rappel the route from its anchors back to the ground.
targets.name: Bishop’s Most Wanted

targets.approach: Follow the well-kept Wapama Falls trail around Hetch Hetchy Reservoir, and the slab lies some distance before Rancheria Falls. The last stretch up to the base is a steep bushwhack along faint deer trails, and poison oak is common even beside the main trails. The girdle begins at a big pine at the slab's left end; an easy fourth-class ramp leads to the slab itself.
targets.descent_text: The line ends at a large pine tree; exit down a small vegetated ramp or gully.
targets.name: Rancheria lower girdle
